descriptions.rgb: Across the five frames, the camera wearer is on a rocky ledge beside a steep rock wall, with a blue rope running vertically near the viewpoint and loose rope coiled on the ground. In frames 1–2, the camera points mostly downward: the wearer’s lower body or gear is partly visible at the bottom edge, and the wall and rope are within arm’s reach, while no other person is clearly visible. In frame 3, about five people stand roughly 1–4 m in front and to the right near the wall; they are about 0.5–2 m apart, several face left or toward the rock, and none clearly looks directly at the camera. In frame 4, the group remains about 1–4 m away but shifts toward the left half of the view as the camera turns right; one helmeted person at roughly 1–2 m is side-on with an arm extended toward the wall or rope, while others stand behind and to that person’s right and are partly mutually occluded. In frame 5, the camera faces farther right and upward along the sloping wall, placing most of the group out of view to the left; a blue rope rises from near the bottom center to a climber approximately 8–12 m ahead and several metres above the wearer, with another small, partly visible person near the upper-right edge. Overall, the sequence changes from a close downward view of the ledge and rope, through a rightward view of the nearby group, to an upward-right view of the more distant climber.
